title: Photo Duo 031 · USSBBW × 애슬리트 USSBBW · 둘 다 정면
prompt:
Image format: a vertical portrait-orientation photograph, 2:3 aspect ratio, taller than it is wide.

A photograph of TWO women standing side by side on a plain seamless deep-charcoal backdrop, nothing else in the frame, the camera set close so the two of them fill the frame edge to edge, 50mm lens at f/8, a single hard key light raking in from one side — a real photograph, not an illustration, not CGI, not a render.

Subjects: TWO real adult women, both far beyond any real person in size, standing square to the camera with their feet planted far apart, their two bodies together so wide that they overflow the full width of the frame and are cut off by the left and right edges, pressed shoulder to shoulder with their sides squeezed against each other and the flesh bulging out where they touch.

Left woman: a Korean woman in her late 50s, warm ivory skin with a golden undertone, her face exactly the same tone as her body, long micro braids to her hips. An immense mass of soft heavy fat sits on her middle, so much of it that it hangs far lower than it projects — sagging down toward her knees under its own weight rather than pushing forward, gathering into three or four heavy rounded folds stacked one above the other, deep creases between them, never taut, never smooth, never round like a drum, merging seamlessly into her sides, hips and thighs with no boundary anywhere, not pregnant. A gigantic bust above it, no waist at all, colossal hips more than three times the width of her shoulders and an enormous rounded rear, each thigh thicker than a normal woman's waist, very thick upper arms. Painted in Korean eunipsa silver inlay — a deep black ground with thick bright silver linework and fine lattice fills, a bold silver band following every deep crease, catching the light the way paint on skin does rather than like real metal.

Right woman: a South Asian woman in her late 30s, rich warm brown skin with golden undertones, her face exactly the same tone as her body, waist-length straight hair. The body of a world's strongest woman pushed far past real limits: enormously broad thick shoulders, massive heavy arms so thick they cannot lie flat against her sides, a colossal bust, a huge barrel torso, no waist at all. A great mass of soft heavy fat sits on her middle, so much of it that it hangs far lower than it projects — sagging down toward her knees under its own weight rather than pushing forward, gathering into two or three heavy rounded folds stacked one above the other, deep creases between them, never taut, never smooth, never round like a drum, merging seamlessly into her sides, hips and thighs with no boundary anywhere, not pregnant. Colossal wide hips and a huge rounded powerful rear, tree-trunk thighs. The muscle is huge but rounded and buried under a thick layer of soft fat, broad blunt swells with no sharp separation. Painted in Mexican Talavera — a glossy white tin glaze painted with cobalt blue, marigold yellow, terracotta orange and green rosettes, star medallions and scalloped borders, a thick cobalt border following every curve.

Their outer arms are held away from their bodies with a visible gap of background at each side. On both: real photographic skin with visible pores, creases where the flesh folds and faint stretch marks, no illustration finish, no CG sheen. The paint is pigment on living skin, distorting over every bulge and cracking where it folds, covering everything below the jaw with no bare skin left; their faces unpainted, the pattern fading out at the neck. Neither arm crosses in front of her own body or the other woman's, both faces toward the camera. Every fold keeps its own rounded outline with a deep crease between them, never one shapeless mass; arms, hands and legs in correct proportion. Both wear extreme platform stiletto heels with soles as tall as their ankle bones.

Vertical 2:3 portrait-orientation photograph, taller than it is wide.
